notes: Main disagreements: (1) phase, mostly general vs before-course vs course-start vs during-work. Resolved by what the passage does: set-up of a statement, tool, website, workshop or contract is before-course; a rule on the students' work (template ban or permission, referral when stuck) is during-work; principles and cautions are general. (2) unit_stance on disclosure and verification conditions in the permit templates (permit vs require): resolved to require where the template says students must or need to state, document, cite or verify; bias and copyright awareness sentences are neutral; the 'if I detect misuse' sentences in the permit templates are restrict. (3) policy_type: the sentence-level choices (P03 vs P118 for 'exercise caution', P91 vs P09 for editing tools, P124 vs P81 for misconduct precedents, P66 vs P09/P36 for informing students of misconduct forms, P116 vs P29 for responsibility for learning, P76 vs P17 for the admissions chatbot, P56 vs P115 for the CIO guidelines, P111 vs UNCOVERED for the honor code, P50 vs P65 for identifiable-data caution) were resolved from the passage and recorded in fit_notes; the orientation integrity discussion and the BOG statute change stay UNCOVERED. In wayne-2, A coded the cheating definition as P01 and B as P36 and the advance-authorization clause as P107 vs P06; final is P36 for the definition and P107 for the clause. (4) actor on remarks reported from campus partners, resolved by who the sentence addresses (instructor for sanctions and online-course regulation; admin for committee voice; all for general observations). (5) modality on hedged needs and intentions (informs vs should vs must). (6) Alignment: five coder pairs that the anchor-position match had linked wrongly were split or re-paired by hand, and a few units that the two coders anchored on different sentences of the same passage were treated as matched. Only-A units (18, e.g. reported student AI uses, terms-of-use caution, graduate-admissions expectations, retention of the BOG statute idea) and only-B units (23, e.g. graduate-template repeats, orientation emphasis, HR/IT operational uses, Libraries research guide, the syllabus-authority clause in wayne-2) were all checked against the source and kept; none was dropped. Stance matched on both documents (wayne-1 delegates, wayne-2 restrict). new_types empty on both sides.
